newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Some want S.Europe sidelined from euro - Portugal.
newsitem.headline: Some want S.Europe sidelined from euro - Portugal.

text.p: Some European banks fear competition from southern Europe and do not want the region to join the launch of a single European currency, Portuguese Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said.

"There are banking institutions that want to sideline countries in southern Europe from the single currency," Sousa Franco told reporters on Tuesday night on the sidelines of a two-day summit in the Azores between the prime ministers of Spain and Portugal.

"I am referring to very defined interests in these institutions that want to have a zone within the euro (single currency) that has no competition from financial institutions and economies in the south of Europe," Sousa Franco said.

The minister did not identify the institutions, but he did say that he believed that the Bundesbank was not against the inclusion of southern European countries in the European single currency, or euro, due to be launched in January 1999.

Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar and his Portuguese counterpart Antonio Guterres were expected to pledge later on Wednesday their determination to lead their countries into the first group joining the euro.
